title: Handle a missing value

outcomes.can: Supply a fallback for a missing value with ??.
Keep empty text and zero separate from a missing value.
Say why an int cannot be null and how int? differs.
Read through two levels that may each be missing.

intro: Sometimes there is no value: a task with no owner, a card with no due date. C# calls that null. This module covers marking a value that may be missing, checking it before use, and supplying a fallback.

steps.title: null means no value
steps.text: null means a variable refers to nothing. string? owner = null; declares a string that may be missing. The ? after the type is a promise to readers and tools that null is allowed here, and editors use it to warn you when you use such a value without a check. Using a member of null, such as owner.Length, stops the program with a NullReferenceException. Test first with owner == null or owner != null. The ?? operator supplies a fallback: owner ?? "Unassigned" is owner when it has a value and "Unassigned" when it is null. The ?. operator reads a member only when there is a value. owner?.Length is null when owner is null, and no exception is thrown.

steps.title: Predict a fallback
steps.text: owner is null. Predict the first two lines of output.

steps.title: Follow the operators
steps.text: owner is null, so owner ?? "Unassigned" gives the fallback. On the next line owner?.Length is null because there is no string to measure, and ?? 0 turns that into 0. No member of null was ever used, so nothing was thrown.

steps.title: Empty is not missing
steps.text: blank holds a string with no characters. Predict the third line of output.

steps.title: Keep real values
steps.text: "" is a real string, so ?? leaves it alone and the comparison prints True. The same holds for numbers. An int always has a value and can never be null. int? is a different type that holds either an int or null. due.HasValue is False while due is null. After due = 0; it holds a real 0, and due ?? -1 gives 0, not the fallback. Zero and empty text are values. Only null means missing.

steps.title: Give an int no value
steps.text: Line 1 assigns null to a plain int. Read the example before checking.

steps.title: Read the compiler error
steps.text: Check the example. CS0037 says null cannot be converted to int because int is a non-nullable value type. If a number can be missing, declare it as int?.

steps.title: Label the owner
steps.text: The starter stops with an exception for a missing owner and gives the wrong label for an empty one. Repair it.

steps.title: Describe a due date
steps.text: Work from the prompt. A missing number and the number 0 mean different things here.

questions.prompt: What are the first two lines of output?

choices.feedback: owner is null, so both fallbacks are used.

choices.text: Unassigned, then the program stops with an error
choices.feedback: ?. reads Length only when there is a value, so nothing is thrown.
null is not empty text. ?? replaces it with the fallback.

questions.prompt: What is the third line of output?

choices.feedback: "" is a real value, so ?? keeps it and the result equals "".
?? replaces only null. An empty string is kept.
The line prints the result of a comparison, which is True or False.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.feedback: null is not turned into 0. An int cannot be given null at all.
The file does not compile, so nothing prints.

choices.text: The compiler reports an error on line 1.
choices.feedback: int always holds a number. Assigning null to it is CS0037.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one operator each. They do not separate null from empty text and zero.
